newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ industry groups turn down NZ$100 mln from govt.
newsitem.headline: NZ industry groups turn down NZ$100 mln from govt.

text.p: New Zealand's four main industry associations said on Friday they were turning down an offer from the centre-right coalition government to spend NZ$100 million more on business assistance.
The New Zealand Chambers of Commerce, Employers Federation, Federated Farmers and Manufacturers Federation said they were all seriously concerned about the proposed expenditure.

"This will allow the coalition to reduce its (extra) expenditure in 1997/8 from $1.2 billion to $1.1 billion -- we invite other groups to critically evaluate the quality and priority of expenditure in other parts of the coalition
agreement," the groups said in a joint statement.

"Our industry groups are mindful of the inflationary impact of higher government spending, and the adverse impact of inflation on our members. Only top priority expenditure that cannot be met from within existing programmes should be considered."

The proferred extra spending included $50 million to the Export Guarantee Fund, $10 million to a venture capital fund, $5 million for export agency Tradenz and $32 million for organic farming research and technology transfer.
The groups said the government would encourage much more investment in jobs and growth by spending the NZ$100 million on tax cuts rather than poorly thought-through handouts.
